text:
rajesh: Heads-up — on long-context load tests (32k/100k windows) we're seeing KV cache memory creep + fragmentation for the gpt-xxl profile. Memory grows ~1.9x over 2M tokens and doesn't reclaim between sessions. Posting a short profile dump and ideas.

mike: Can you paste the top alloc histogram?

rajesh: copied roughs: lots of tiny free runs (<512B) and a non-trivial count of 4k holes. Bin mismatch: many KV entries are ~1.1–3.5k after metadata, so they don't fit neatly into 4k aligned slabs.

sara: Wait, are we still using 4k base blocksize for the KV slab? I thought we prototyped 2k once.

lina: Yesterday's run: switching blocksize 4k -> 2k reduced external fragmentation from ~18% to ~9%, but increased metadata overhead by ~3%. No measurable throughput drop on p50/p95 for most traces.

rajesh: That's promising. But the bigger issue is holes from evictions + alignment — we leave many medium-sized runs that can't be reused for slightly larger entries. Proposal: compaction pass that coalesces adjacent free runs when free fraction > threshold.

mike: +1 for background compaction. We need a CPU-budgeted strategy so we don't regress tail latency. Maybe run when CPU idle or in small time-slices.

sara: Another angle: change binning scheme to variable-sized buckets (sub-4k buckets) so small slices can sit in small bins and avoid stealing space from medium entries. Mixed freelist.

lina: Quick compaction trigger prototype I sketched: 
```
if free_bytes_ratio > 0.12 and contiguous_free_runs > 64:
    schedule_compaction(background=True, budget_ms=20)
```
This keeps compaction short and only when fragmentation likely to matter.

mike: Also track largest_free_run and prefer evicting entries that create large contiguous runs. Eviction policy + compaction coordination could reduce churn.

rajesh: I also thought about owner-tagged reuse: allow opportunistic reuse of small holes across contexts if we tag entries with owner bits and validate on placement. That reduces wasted slots but needs safety checks.

sara: Owner-tagging seems ok — we already have model+seq metadata per entry. We can add a tombstone / relocation bit to speed coalesce without full memcpy.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: kv-allocator-v2 -> canary on 2026-03-10 03:22 UTC (release notes: compaction trigger + owner-tag proto).

rajesh: Plan from here: prototype compaction pass + owner-tagging, add metrics: `free_run_count`, `avg_run_len`, `largest_free_run`, `compaction_runs`, and measure p99 mem delta. I'll open draft PR with perf test plan.

mike: Also add an eviction hook to prefer reclaiming contiguous large runs first (score by potential contiguous_bytes reclaimed).

lina: I'll run a 100k-token nightly pass with allocator-v2 and post numbers tomorrow morning. Will include histos and heap snapshots.

sara: One small caveat: avoid heavy memcpy during compaction. Prefer pointer swap / relocation table where possible or do compaction incrementally.

rajesh: Yep — incremental compaction with relocation table is acceptable. Will try to keep per-iteration CPU budget < 20ms.

mike: SGTM :thumbsup:

sara: Thanks — if the canary looks good we can roll to staging and then prod.

rajesh: Opening PR now (WIP). Will ping this thread with numbers and the PR link.
